finalWindowVerdict.detail: Window 3's buyer could not buy: 1 purchase attempt(s), every one of them failed, no single issuer held the 10000 mSIU the job needs (largest: 32000 mSIU), and ORCHESTRATOR had secured nothing ahead. This is the scarcity finding. Note that the window still reports passed=true: a gate was delivered anyway, by WORKER-CODE, without the work ever being paid for. That says nothing about the instrument and must not be read as it working.

verdictAnnotations.correctedBy: spec §4.6af — the final-window classifier could not see a dollar purchase
verdictAnnotations.whyStoredIsWrong: `purchaseSucceeded` was satisfied only by a mint_claim/pay_with_claim capacity event attributed to the buyer. A USDC payment produces neither: `pay` opens an escrow, and the `reserve_for_work` it leads to is attributed to the SELLER, who commits the capacity. ORCHESTRATOR's window-3 payment settled — this same record carries it, in `windows[2].purchases.decisions` and in the `assetChoice` line "ORCHESTRATOR: 1 in USDC" — so the attempt was counted while its success was invisible, and the scarcity branch fired by construction. The stored detail contradicts itself in one sentence: "no single issuer held the 10000 mSIU the job needs (largest: 32000 mSIU)".
verdictAnnotations.whyItSurvivedNineRuns: Every final-window purchase before this run settled in fSIU (the §4.6f artefact), so the dollar branch was never exercised. This is the first run bought in dollars in a final window and the only run ever to report scarcity. The classifier was correct only while the bias held.
verdictAnnotations.readTheStoredVerdictAs: a scoring defect, not a finding. No scarcity occurred in this run: the pool ended whole at 80,000/80,000, verified on chain from a fresh connection after the process exited.
